posts.title: When to Throw the Party - A Platform Engineering Problem
posts.description: It's obvious that the DevOps movement destroyed the cultural phenomenon of Release Parties, where Engineering and Product finally came together after a stressful season of crunch, blame and broken promises to get drunk together after the first successful yet random build. At the same time the Ops guys shaved an ever-growing herd of yaks to deploy that particular build in production before daylight

posts.title: Meeting Guidelines are institutional Theater
posts.description: Back in 2007 when I started in IT, receiving a meeting invite was a highlight. Somebody took notice of me and, maybe, even considered me valuable in one way or another. Turns out, most invites we receive in the workplace are actually pretty much the contrary. I) Your boss (or/and his boss) will never read nor care for your organization's meeting guidelines.
